title: POC Weekly - Redwood Private VPC Pilot Sync
meeting_header: Date: 2026-05-01 | Time: 11:00 AM PT | Duration: 55m | Location: Zoom | Attendees: Alex Chen, Priya Nair, Jamal Ortiz, Lee Park (Redwood) — Sara Lopez, Mark Dunn, Priyanka Rao, Ben Holt (Atlas Analytics)
summary: Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) pilot. Reviewed network peering progress, routing issues discovered during perf runs, nightly upgrade plan for runtime 2.3.1, and next steps for security questionnaire and benchmark artifacts. Action items assigned for security workbook, perf logs, and peering ticket follow-up.
next_steps: Alex to share upgraded runtime changelog and rollout window by 2026-05-04
Priya to upload perf logs and KV-cache traces to shared drive by tomorrow
Mark to confirm peering CIDR and open ticket with networking by 2026-05-03
Sara to review security workbook and call out any gaps by 2026-05-08
action_items: Alex Chen: send runtime 2.3.1 changelog and proposed maintenance window - due 2026-05-04
Priya Nair: upload perf logs, KV cache dumps, and the benchmark spreadsheet - due 2026-05-02
Mark Dunn: confirm VPC peering CIDR ranges and open support ticket for routing mismatch - due 2026-05-03
Priyanka Rao: compile answers to the encryption/KMS and audit log questions and share - due 2026-05-08
transcript:
00:00 Alex Chen: ok good morning everyone, thanks for joining. we're gonna run through the weekly pilot status for the Redwood Privat V P C pilot. we've got about 55 minutes on the calendar. Sara, Mark, Priyanka, Ben, you all good?
00:13 Sara Lopez: yeah morning, all good. got my calendar up. thanks.
00:17 Priya Nair: quick intro, I'm Priya from Redwood, SE on the project, i'll handle the perf bits and the runtime upgrade notes.
00:23 Mark Dunn: Mark from infra, i'll speak to peering and network. we had that weird routing flap in the test cluster last night.
00:29 Ben Holt: Ben, ml eng, will run through the inference perf numbers you sent over.
00:34 Alex Chen: great, quick agenda: networking status, perf run review, runtime upgrade plan (2.3.1), security questions, then recap/next steps. sound ok?
00:44 Sara Lopez: yes.
00:46 Alex Chen: Mark, can you start with the networking/peering update?
00:51 Mark Dunn: sure. so peering is 95% done, we established the transit gateway, route tables are populated but we hit a routing mismatch where some traffic to the inference nodes was hitting the NAT gateway instead of the internal route, that's why you saw elevated egress in the perf runs. i filed ticket with our networking team.
01:12 Priya Nair: hmm yeah that would explain the latency spikes. when the NAT path is used we also see connection setup overhead and TCP retransmits. did you have asymmetric routes or overlapping CIDRs?
01:23 Mark Dunn: overlapping CIDR on one of the test VPCs - i didn't catch that in the initial mapping, so a subset of pods got the wrong next hop. fixing that now.
01:31 Alex Chen: ok good, action item for Mark to confirm the final CIDRs and the ticket number. can you put that in the channel?
01:37 Mark Dunn: will do.
01:39 Ben Holt: quick perf note - we ran the baseline against runtime 2.2.8 yesterday and then re-ran after the peering change. median latency for the 512 token seq increased to 210ms p50 from 150ms when the NAT path was used, p95 went to 480ms. throughput dropped ~18%.
02:01 Priya Nair: those numbers line up with the connection overhead - when the KV cash prefix cache was cold and the traffic went via NAT we saw additional round trips. also, small note, the transcript exporter sometimes shows "KV cash" instead of KV cache, so ignore the typos in the sheet.
02:15 Ben Holt: lol yes, i saw KV cash in the spreadsheet, i thought that was a new feature.
02:18 Sara Lopez: are these runs synthetic or using our production prompt mix?
02:22 Ben Holt: synthetic plus a sample of production prompts (about 10% of the production mix) - we tried to match token distribution.
02:30 Priya Nair: ok, on the perf side we also noticed a suboptimal kernel selection for the 8k context variant in 2.2.8. runtime 2.3.1 includes a kernel selector patch and improved attention tiling, which should reduce p50 by about 15% in our internal tests. the patch also improves continuous batching heuristics for low-latency workloads.
02:52 Jamal Ortiz: (SRE) one caveat: the 2.3.1 rolling upgrade touches the compile cache and requires a short warmup window per node. best practice is a staged canary across a small subset of nodes during low-traffic hours.
03:07 Alex Chen: what's the maintenance window you're proposing?
03:10 Priya Nair: we propose a 2-hour window during the night in your timezone, canary 10% of nodes for 30 minutes, then ramp. we have an automatic rollback if latency regresses beyond your SLO.
03:23 Sara Lopez: night window sounds fine, our critical batch jobs run at 2am local, so maybe 4am? we prefer 4-6am.
03:33 Alex Chen: noted. Alex to propose exact dates.
03:36 Priyanka Rao: security question - will this upgrade affect the control plane or require outbound access to redwood.cloud endpoints? our compliance team requires limited egress for package fetch.
03:48 Priya Nair: good question. the runtime binary in 2.3.1 is self-contained; we don't need outbound access for normal operation. the upgrade process will pull an artifact from our repo if you want us to manage the rollout; we can also provide an air-gapped bundle and a signed artifact for manual install.
04:05 Priyanka Rao: ok please send the signed artifact option, and the hash, we need to verify.
04:10 Alex Chen: noted - include sha256 and the signed bundle.
04:13 Mark Dunn: another networking detail - the peering change fixed the NAT path for most traffic but we still have a subset of traffic coming from an older route table associated with the test nodes. i'm rolling a quick ebs snapshot and then migrating the node group to the new route table.
04:29 Ben Holt: on another note, we captured KV-cache hit rates - cold start hit rate was 6% and after 20 minutes warmed to 62% in the happy path, but when the NAT hit we saw KV hits drop to 28% which led to extra tokens generated and higher CPU on the GPU side.
04:50 Priya Nair: thanks, that's helpful. we'll correlate that with the allocator metrics and the KV-cache logs you uploaded. can you confirm which log bundle you uploaded to the share? i saw perf-logs-0501-v1.zip.
05:02 Ben Holt: yes perf-logs-0501-v1.zip, includes the pprof and tcpdump samples.
05:07 Alex Chen: perfect. Priya, will runtime 2.3.1 change the KV-cache format or the prefix caching behavior?
05:13 Priya Nair: no format change, just smarter warmup and a small compacting change to reduce memory fragmentation. migration is transparent in-place.
05:23 Sara Lopez: any impact on model compatibility or quantization profiles? we're using the 4-bit quant with a custom quant config.
05:31 Priya Nair: 2.3.1 preserves quant configs; we did some additional quantization-friendly optimizations, but we recommend testing on a canary model before the full fleet.
05:41 Ben Holt: we have a custom config for Q4 bits; i can run a short canary tomorrow against 2.3.1 if you provide the artifact.
05:49 Alex Chen: action - Priya provide canary artifact and short runbook; Ben to run canary.
05:55 Priyanka Rao: question on audit logs: does the private deployment push audit logs to our SIEM or store them in the customer-managed s3? we need to ensure retention and immutability.
06:05 Jamal Ortiz: we can stream audit logs to your S3 bucket with SSE-KMS encryption, or we can push via your syslog/forwarder. retention policy is configurable on your side. you can enable write-once options via object lock if you need immutability.
06:20 Priyanka Rao: ok please include the S3 stream config in the security workbook.
06:24 Alex Chen: noted - we'll update workbook.
06:26 Sara Lopez: quick procurement question - if we go to Dedicated later how hard is it to lift and shift from Private?
06:33 Priya Nair: the API and routing are identical, most customers do a lift-and-shift and pin the exact model version. Dedicated is more of a capacity contract change; we'll help with model snapshots and migrations.
06:44 Mark Dunn: back to peering - i'll confirm the CIDRs in the channel. we did notice a small MTU mismatch on the overlay which caused fragmentation, i increased it to 9001 and that reduced retransmits.
06:58 Alex Chen: nice, good find.
07:00 Ben Holt: a question for Priya - the benchmark spreadsheet shows a p95 outlier at 1.2s for a particular prompt; is that an artifact of one long-tail model eval or something in the network?
07:12 Priya Nair: looking at the pcap it shows a stall waiting on TCP ack, so likely network retransmit. not the model.
07:19 Ben Holt: ok good to know, we'll re-run after Mark's routing fix.
07:23 Alex Chen: timeline check - runtime 2.3.1 canary target this week if peering is stable. Priya, can you send the canary artifact today?
07:31 Priya Nair: yes i'll upload the signed artifact and short runbook by EOD.
07:35 Alex Chen: Mark to confirm CIDR and the ticket number by Monday morning.
07:40 Mark Dunn: i'll post ticket NET-4521 and CIDRs in the channel.
07:44 Priyanka Rao: security workbook items - i'll need the SHA, the S3 bucket config, and the PKI signing cert.
07:51 Jamal Ortiz: we can share the public signing cert and the signed bundle; for PKI integration we support customer-managed KMS and HSM via our keywrap option.
07:59 Sara Lopez: perfect. any blockers from Redwood side?
08:03 Alex Chen: none immediate - perf impacts are explained and we have mitigations. main open items are peering confirmation, signed artifact, perf logs correlation.
08:15 Ben Holt: one more note - we saw a small regression on token pricing when we tried a different micro-batching heuristic in 2.2.8; how are you surfacing cost implications in these rollouts?
08:28 Priya Nair: Redwood Optimize will produce a cost delta report for the canary if you enable the costing hooks; we can toggle batching heuristics during canary and capture cost vs latency metrics.
08:40 Sara Lopez: yes please turn that on for our canary.
08:44 Alex Chen: noted. we'll enable cost delta capture.
08:48 Priya Nair: i'll also include a short checklist for rollback criteria - CPU/gpu utilization, p50/p95 regressions, and cost thresholds.
08:58 Alex Chen: going to recap - action items: Alex will share proposed maintenance window and dates; Priya to upload signed artifact, runbook, and perf logs correlation by EOD; Mark to confirm CIDRs and NET-4521; Priyanka to gather security answers; Ben to run canary once artifact is available. any additions?
09:20 Sara Lopez: please add the benchmark spreadsheet link in the recap.
09:24 Alex Chen: good call - will include links.
09:27 Sara Lopez: ok thanks everyone - that covers it for us.
09:30 Alex Chen: thanks team, next sync same time next week unless we need an extra canary call. we'll follow-up in the channel. bye.
09:34 Meeting end: 00:55:12
notes: Peering issue caused NAT egress path and latency spikes; overlapping CIDR fixed pending confirmation
Runtime 2.3.1 expected to improve p50 by ~15% and batching heuristics; upgrade plan agreed with canary and rollback criteria
Security will get signed artifact and S3 streaming config; audit logs to customer-managed S3 with SSE-KMS supported
